# CBOR and LDOR {.unnumbered #cbor-and-ldor}

## Rank-1 channel: CBOR {#cbor}

The rank-1 vector polarizability couples to atomic orientation. Its dispersive part distinguishes the two circular optical components and produces circular birefringence optical rotation (CBOR). Its absorptive part describes circular dichroism.

## Rank-2 channel: LDOR {#ldor}

The rank-2 tensor polarizability couples to atomic alignment. It produces linear birefringence and linear-dichroism optical rotation (LDOR), depending on the relative orientation of the input polarization and the atomic alignment axes.

CBOR and LDOR are not inserted as two independent rotation angles. They first produce changes in the transmitted Stokes vector.

## Rotation from Stokes parameters {#rotation-from-stokes}

For ellipse azimuth (phi) and ellipticity angle (chi),

$$
s_1=\cos(2\chi)\cos(2\phi),\qquad
s_2=\cos(2\chi)\sin(2\phi),\qquad
s_3=\sin(2\chi).
$$

Linearization gives

$$
\delta\phi=
\frac12
\frac{s_1\delta s_2-s_2\delta s_1}
{s_1^2+s_2^2}.
$$

Thus both CBOR and LDOR are included through their contributions to (delta s_1) and (delta s_2). For an initially linear beam on a Stokes axis, this reduces to (delta\phi=\delta s_2/(2s_1)).

## Weak and physical-pump totals {#cbor-ldor-total}

For a weak detector, orientation and alignment readout operators add at the complex-susceptibility level before amplitude is taken.

For a physical pump, Total is obtained by closing the full rank-1 plus rank-2 feedback together. The displayed Orientation-induced and Alignment-induced curves are separately closed counterfactuals. Therefore, they generally do not add to Total. See the [feedback closure](uniform-density-matrix-feedback.qmd#feedback-closure).
